text: Did A press the eraser against the paper to make indentations that would reveal the message when the paper was shaded?
Did A make the message by removing or altering something already on the paper, rather than by adding a substance?
Did the eraser itself leave a visible mark on the paper?
Was the message visible on the paper immediately after A used the eraser?
Did A use the eraser to transfer a marking substance onto the paper?
Was the message readable only under a particular angle or lighting condition?
Did rubbing the eraser cause the paper itself to change color through heat?
Was the message encoded in the eraser’s shape or surface before A used it?
Did contact with the eraser make the message visible through a chemical change, rather than a physical or optical effect?
Did rubbing the eraser abrade or roughen parts of the paper, creating the visible message through a difference in surface texture?
Did A form the message from crumbs produced by rubbing the eraser on the paper?
Did A use the eraser to manipulate a separate object or material that then produced the message on the paper?
Did A arrange multiple separate objects on the paper so that their placement itself spelled out the message?
Did A use the eraser to physically actuate a mechanism that caused another object or material to produce the message?
Did A use the eraser to hold or position a separate material that directly produced the message on the paper?
Did the separate material A manipulated produce the visible message by depositing pigment or ink on the paper?
Was the separate material a liquid?
